descriptionChirho: The ancient city of Sodom, referenced in the NT as a paradigmatic example of divine judgment against wickedness (Mt 10:15; 11:23-24; Lk 10:12; 17:29; Rom 9:29; 2 Pet 2:6; Jude 1:7; Rev 11:8). All 10 occurrences are the same indeclinable proper noun in different syntactic functions (genitive, dative, nominative). Multilingual forms are consistent: Spanish 'Sódoma/Sodoma'; Hindi 'सदोम/सोदोम'; Arabic 'سَدومَ/سَدُومَ/سدوم' are merely vocalization variants of the same name; Korean '소돔' is uniform; Swahili 'Sodoma' is consistent throughout. The three clusters represent purely case-syntactic splits (of-Sodom, to/for-Sodom, Sodom as subject) of a single proper noun, not distinct senses.
